articles.title: $25 million for 30,000 drones: Ukraine’s new plan to turn porn into war cash sparks controversy
articles.description: Ukraine is considering a controversial new source of wartime cash as its battle against Russia drains state finances. According to The Wall Street Journal, lawmakers are weighing legalising pornography, potentially generating up to $25 million in taxes—enough for roughly 30,000 drones. The proposal comes amid a bizarre contradiction: adult creators can face prosecution despite tax authorities pursuing their earnings. Nearly 7,900 Ukrainian creators reportedly made more than $131 million through OnlyFans in 2023. With another difficult winter of fighting looming, could Ukraine's booming underground adult-content economy become an unlikely source of funding for Zelensky's drone war?

articles.title: Merz stumped as pro-Putin AfD storms to victory? German Chancellor’s 1st reaction after poll shocker
articles.description: Friedrich Merz has delivered a stark response to the AfD's historic Saxony-Anhalt election result, admitting Germany had reached a “turning point” after his CDU suffered what he called its most serious defeat in decades. But the Chancellor also pointed east, saying there was “particular delight” 2,500 kilometres away and warning that Russia seeks to destabilise the West. Merz vowed he would not “budge one millimeter” on supporting Ukraine despite the electoral shock and promised fundamental reforms at home. With voters delivering a devastating verdict, can Merz keep confronting Putin without further strengthening the AfD?

articles.title: 'Shameful': Singapore Probes Anti-Indian Hate Wave, Racism With China Link Under Scanner
articles.description: Singapore is probing racist comments aimed at Indians after Nepal floods and an Air India funding row. Senior Minister K Shanmugam called the abuse shameful and unacceptable. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong warned that hate must not become normal. The comments used slurs and attacked Indian-origin executives linked to Air India. In June, Singapore blocked 14 anti-Indian posts. Its Home Affairs Ministry said they likely came from a China-based platform and sought to inflame racial tension. Why are Indians targeted? Is India facing a new information war? Can online hate damage Singapore’s model? This India-focused report examines racism, foreign influence, Air India, Singapore and the fight to stop hostile narratives from turning a business debate and a disaster into an attack on an entire community. It asks who amplifies the anger and who benefits from distrust.
